close_reason: Renamed ParseResult to CalendarEventParseResult across backend.rs (definition + impl + new() ctor + rustdoc), lib.rs re-export, README.md, and PLAN.md. The object-prefix naming now mirrors the canonical mail-server's MdnParseResult precedent. Also cleaned up the 'locked sister crate' rustdoc phrasing per the updated workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template banner wording. fmt/clippy/test/doc all green.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:581 exposes `pub struct ParseResult` for `CalendarEvent/parse`.

The canonical sibling jmap-mail-server names its parse-result struct `MdnParseResult` (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mdn.rs:44) — object-prefix naming that is unambiguous when multiple `*-server` extension crates are `use`d together.

Calendars-server's bare `ParseResult` collides with the generic concept. A consumer importing both crates with `use jmap_calendars_server::ParseResult; use jmap_mail_server::MdnParseResult;` works today, but if a future extension's parse result also lands as plain `ParseResult` (the cookie-cutter divergence is invisible to a future contributor reading only this crate), the names clash on `use`.

The rustdoc at backend.rs:577 even cites `MdnParseResult` as its precedent: "Mirrors the `MdnParseResult` precedent in the locked sister crate jmap-mail-server" — yet picked a name that does NOT mirror.

What callers cannot rely on:
- That `use jmap_calendars_server::ParseResult` will not shadow or collide with a future sibling crate's type of the same bare name.
- That the workspace cookie-cutter naming rule is followed here (it is not).

Rename to `CalendarEventParseResult` to match the sibling pattern. Doing so once shipped is a SemVer break; pre-1.0 the rename is free.

If the rename is rejected as bikeshedding, the alternative is to fix the canonical mail-server to rename `MdnParseResult` to the bare `ParseResult` pattern AND propagate — but that contradicts the existing locked-canonical posture (mail-server is the canonical, not calendars).
title: ParseResult name collides with the generic concept; sibling MdnParseResult uses object-prefix naming
